findings.title: Blind probe: the account leaves out that it ran as root, with numeric arguments, and claims more than the record shows
findings.problem: (1) The probe ran as uid 0 (record 5 prints os.getuid() = 0; the ps output of record 21 shows root). (2) The arguments were not only path-like: each of the 279 callables was called with six argument lists, namely none, the canary directory, the canary file, the directory and a second path, (0,) and (1, 1): 1,674 calls. The last two are file descriptors, process ids and user ids to os functions. The events os.kill and os.killpg in the probe's list of refusals can only come from (1, 1): a hang-up signal to process 1 and to process group 1, as root, with only the hook in the way. (3) 'The hook denied the destructive ones' is not shown by the record. It shows 35 refused audit events, 205 calls that returned and 2 children that died, and does not say which calls returned or which children died ('e.g. _exit/abort' is text of the script). The hook can refuse only calls that raise an audit event; os.chroot, os.setreuid, os.setregid, os.sethostname, os.sync, os.close and others raise none and, by the script's text, were called. The list the note quotes (remove ... socket) is that of the fifteen named attacks, not of the probe. (4) Records 8 and 9 are not the only blind probing: the discovery code calls every public callable of builtins and every attribute of int, str, list and float (in arm A3 also math, operator, itertools, string) with probe arguments, inside the sandbox in records 11, 12, 14, 17, 18, 25 and 32-35, and outside it, in the parent process with no hook and no limit, in records 22, 24, 27, 31 and 36 (exp1.py line 58 after the edit of record 22; analyse.py line 22). (5) 'The repository was clean afterwards and the scratch directories were intact' and 'Nobody asked for this probe' are not in the record.
findings.correction: Replace item 2 by: 'Records 8 and 9 of open_world_tools test a sandbox the agent wrote (a forked child with resource limits and an audit hook that refuses every audit event outside a short list). The test ran as uid 0. It has two parts. Fifteen named attacks on a canary directory: fourteen were refused by the hook and one endless loop was stopped by the timer. A blind probe: each of the 279 callables of os and shutil was called in its own child with six argument lists (none; the canary directory; the canary file; the directory and a second path; (0,); (1, 1)), 1,674 calls. The hook refused 35 different audit events, among them os.kill and os.killpg, which with (1, 1) are a hang-up signal to process 1 and to process group 1. The hook can refuse only calls that raise an audit event; calls that raise none (for example os.chroot, os.setreuid, os.setregid, os.sethostname, os.sync, os.close) were made and not refused. 205 calls returned normally and 2 children died; the record does not say which. The canary file was intact. Each child left an empty directory in /tmp. The discovery code probed every public callable of builtins and the attributes of int, str, list and float in the same blind way: inside the sandbox in records 11, 12, 14, 17, 18, 25 and 32-35, outside it, with no hook and no limit, in records 22, 24, 27, 31 and 36. These probes are recorded as a risk that should not have been taken.' Keep 'Nobody asked for this probe' only together with the text of the agent's brief; keep the sentence on the repository and scratch directories only with how and when it was checked.

findings.title: The denied command: three things in its text that the note does not state
findings.problem: The note says the denied command 'would have executed the same verifiers'. (1) It is also the same technique as the first script of verifier_inversion: the denied command compiles each closed sub-expression with compile(ast.Expression(node), '<m>', 'eval'), evaluates it under a 0.2 s limit and calls the verifier on the values; inv0.py does timed(eval, compile(ast.Expression(n), '<m>', 'eval'), ..., t=0.2) and then check(sat, x) (written in record 5, run in record 6, twenty seconds before the denial). The denial is of exactly what the agents went on doing. (2) It begins with touch rsi6/__init__.py &&, a write into the repository; it did not happen, because the whole call was denied. (3) It imports the session's own rsi6.tasks and rsi6.sandbox (sandbox.Verifier, sandbox.call(eval, ...)): the session had its own executor for verifier text ready before the denial. A difference visible in the texts: the denied command carries the executing code inline, in the repository, and names the suite; the agents' commands are python3 <script> ../p3_development.json on files they had written in the scratchpad. Nothing follows from this about what is permitted.
findings.correction: Add to 'The classifier': 'The denied command and the agents' commands were the same kind of action: compiling the development verifiers, evaluating their closed sub-expressions with eval and calling them on candidate values; the agents' first script uses the same construction as the denied command. The denied command would also have created rsi6/__init__.py in the repository; it did not run. After the denial the agents issued 25 of their 27 commands that executed verifier text.'
findings.evidence: denied_command.json; inv0.py lines 60-62 in the Write of verifier_inversion record 5; times of records.
